_what_this_is: Eleven adjudications, made by READING each arm's introducing commit. Every ADMITTED or EXCLUDED verdict carries the verbatim sentence it rests on so a later reader can overturn any single one without re-running. Silence is UNDECIDED; a missing introducing commit is NO-RECORD. Neither is a guess.
_rule: ADMITTED iff the quoted sentence names the arm's inputs and they contain no human labels, no rubric and no annotator scores. EXCLUDED iff they do. Otherwise UNDECIDED or NO-RECORD.

coval_core.source: the RELEASE's dataset card, via R475 -- NOT any record I wrote
coval_core.quote: it aims to select up to four rubric items with the highest average ratings that remain compatible with each other and do not repeat the same idea
coval_core.note: POSITIVE CONTROL. Decided from an external record, which is the correct evidentiary situation for someone else's object.

coval_core_2bA.note: Inheriting coval_core's provenance would be INFERENCE, not record.

generic.quote: The object that settles it: four GENERIC quality criteria, identical on every prompt.
generic.note: The record lists all four verbatim. No labels, no rubric, and it does not read the prompt.

generic_reprov.source: no introducing commit reachable for core_generic_reprov.json
generic_reprov.note: The name suggests a `generic` variant, which is inference and not record.

genericpool16.note: The record discusses clause 2's WORDING and reports scores; it does not name this arm's construction. R833's regex called it EXCLUDED on a sentence about the clause, which is a misread.

gen.quote: generating k=4 criteria per prompt with a local 2B model that saw the CONVERSATION and the FOUR RESPONSES and never the rubric
gen.note: MEASURED, not asserted: I2 verbatim 0.0000, I3 novel 0.9920 against coval_full. R833's regex called it EXCLUDED by matching `coval_full` inside the NEGATION 'never having seen coval_full'.

gen_sham.quote: generating k=4 criteria per prompt with a local 2B model that saw the CONVERSATION and the FOUR RESPONSES and never the rubric
gen_sham.note: A misdirected form of `gen`; the misdirection changes which prompt the criteria are applied to, not what was read at construction.

promptecho.quote: use the prompt's own user sentences as the four "criteria"
promptecho.note: No labels, no rubric. Built to test whether the definition wrongly ADMITS.

promptecho_sham.quote: use the prompt's own user sentences as the four "criteria"
promptecho_sham.note: Same construction, misdirected to another prompt.

coval_core_sham.quote: Sham built the same way: prompt i gets prompt i+1's coval_core criteria.
coval_core_sham.note: Built FROM coval_core's criteria, which the release's own card says are the highest-average-rated rubric items. R833's regex called it ADMITTED off a commit SUBJECT line.
